rooms.1600: The Path of Heroes begins at a broad arch of weathered stone, its flagstones worn into shallow troughs by the feet of ages. The way south leads back through the white pillars of the gate of Fameland. A cold wind carries a faint hum from somewhere deep in the ruin. The path runs on north between rows of toppled columns, each one carved with a faded laurel.
rooms.1601: Broken columns line both sides of the path here, their fluting chipped and their bases sunk in drifted dust. A cracked basin of black stone stands by the verge, long dry and ringed with old green stain. Grey light falls aslant from a sky the colour of pewter. The path continues north and south through the ruin.
rooms.1602: A great statue of a robed hero stands on a plinth beside the path, its face worn smooth by wind and one stone hand held out with the palm open. Lichen has crept across the carved cloak in orange patches. Faint scratches mark the flagstones where pilgrims once knelt. The path runs north deeper into the ruin and south back the way you came.
rooms.1603: Here the flagstones are cracked and heaved by the roots of thorn bushes that have taken hold in the gaps. Fallen blocks of grey marble lie in heaps beside the path, some still bearing a fragment of carved inscription. A low hum rises and falls, as if the ground itself were breathing. The path goes on north and south.
rooms.1604: The path widens into a paved court that narrows again toward the crossing ahead. Rows of stone plinths stand empty on either side, their statues long since stolen or shattered. Pale pebbles crunch underfoot, and the hum of the rift is plainer here. The Junction of Ancients lies just north, where several ways meet, and the path runs back south.
rooms.1605: Four ways meet at a great round plaza paved in black and white stone, its centre marked by a cracked ring of bronze set flush with the ground. The Way of Ancients leaves north between tall columns, while the Walkway of Bones runs east, pale and strange in the gloom. West the Way of Heroes passes under a line of lofty statues, and the path you came by runs south. The air is heavy with age and the hum of the rift.
rooms.1608: The Way of Ancients is a broad avenue of dark paving, flanked by tall pillars carved with the names of long-dead champions, most of them worn past reading. Wind sighs through gaps in the colonnade. A thin drift of dead leaves has gathered against the plinths. The avenue runs north into the ruin and south back to the plaza of the junction.
rooms.1625: Great urns of weathered bronze stand along the avenue, green with verdigris and dented by some ancient violence. Between them the paving is scored with long gouges, as though something heavy was dragged across it. Pale moss grows in the cracks. The way continues north and south.
rooms.1626: The avenue runs between two rows of columns here, and the roofless sky above is streaked with slow cloud. A broken arch spans the road, one half still standing, the other lying in tumbled blocks. Dust hangs in the slanting light. The Way of Ancients goes on north to a junction and south the way you came.
rooms.1627: At this junction the avenue splits, one arm running east and the other west, while the road you followed ends at a squat stone pedestal. The pedestal is bare, though a ring of chiselled laurel still circles its edge. Cold air slides along the paving from both ways. Dust and fallen pebbles dance in small whirls on the stones, and the way back lies south.
rooms.1644: The avenue runs straight and level between low walls of dark stone half buried in creeping ivy. The paving here is unusually smooth, polished by countless processions. A line of cracked bronze lamps hangs from iron arms, empty of oil for centuries. The junction lies west, and the road goes on east.
rooms.1643: Tall grass and thistles grow thick in the cracks of the paving, bending in the wind that moves along the avenue. A toppled column lies across half the road, its drums rolled apart like coins. The stone beneath is scorched in a long dark stripe. The avenue bends ahead to the east and runs back west toward the junction.
rooms.1642: The avenue turns sharply here, curving from the west toward the north around a round platform of cracked tiles. At its centre a stone basin holds a skin of dark rainwater. Carved reliefs of marching warriors run along the low wall, their faces scoured by weather. The way continues north, and west lies the long straight road you walked.
rooms.1641: Narrow and cold, the avenue here runs between two high walls of fitted blocks, so that only a strip of sky shows overhead. Faded paint clings to the stonework in flecks of red and ochre, the last trace of a victory frieze. Water drips somewhere unseen. The road runs on north and south.
rooms.1640: A line of stone benches borders the avenue, polished smooth by those who once rested here to watch processions pass. Most are cracked, and one has fallen into two halves with a rusted iron spike between them. The wind carries the dry smell of old dust and ash. The road bends ahead to the north and runs south toward the earlier bend.
rooms.1639: The road bends here around a huge fallen head of weathered stone, a heroic face half sunk in the paving. Its blank eyes stare at the sky, and ivy trails across its brow like a wreath of green. The hum of the rift is felt in the soles of your feet. The way leads south along the avenue and west along a straighter stretch.
rooms.1638: The avenue runs between rows of cracked statues, some headless, some armless, all grey with the soot of old fires. A shallow gutter crosses the road, choked with fine silt and the brittle bones of small beasts. The hum of the rift is loud now, a deep and steady note felt in the chest. East the road bends; west it runs toward a gloomy gateway.
rooms.1637: A pair of massive gateposts stands at the road's end, carved with spiralling runes and linked by a lintel cracked clean through. Beyond them lies the dim, shadowed mouth of the Road to the Temple. The air is cooler and smells of stone and distant storms. The avenue returns the way you came, toward the east.
rooms.1636: This is a vaulted hall of grey stone, a long echoing passage where the Way of Ancients runs under a roof. Thick pillars march along both walls, and iron braziers stand cold in the corners. The hum of the rift is strongest here, shivering through the floor. Ways lead east toward the gateposts and west along the avenue, while a broad opening in the south wall leads to the Rift.
rooms.1645: The ground ends in a vast ragged chasm that splits the city, its far lip lost in shadow and a pale light pulsing in its depths. A narrow bridge of fitted stone crosses it to the broad marble stair of the Temple of Garathorm, which rises to the south. The air shakes with the great hum, and a cold wind tugs at your clothes. To the north is the vaulted Road to the Temple.
rooms.1635: The avenue runs on beside a long wall hung with the rust-brown remains of iron shields, their devices eaten away. Underfoot, the paving is cracked and strewn with pale gravel that crunches loudly. A cold draught breathes from the vaulted road to the east. West, the way stretches toward a bend.
rooms.1634: Tall thin pillars stand in pairs along the road, each pair once holding a banner now rotted to nothing but rings of corroded iron. Nests of dry twigs crowd the capitals. The paving is pitted by centuries of rain, and puddles shine in the hollows. The road runs east toward the temple vault and west to a bend.
rooms.1633: The avenue swings from the east toward the south here, curving around a low mound of rubble that was once a tower. Blocks the size of oxen lie half buried in thistles. A line of faint carved stars is still visible on the nearest wall. East lies the straight road toward the temple, and the way south runs on along the avenue.
rooms.1632: Long shadows lie across the road, cast by a row of leaning obelisks inscribed with columns of tiny script. A few have fallen and split. The stone underfoot is cold and slick with dew, and a sour smell of wet earth rises from the gaps. The way goes north to a bend and south along the avenue.
rooms.1631: The road is bordered on one side by a low parapet of white stone, beyond which a sheer drop falls into mist, the edge of some older terrace of the city. Cold fog beads on the stone. Cracks run through the paving like frozen lightning. The avenue goes north and south from here.
rooms.1630: Here the avenue turns, swinging from the north toward the east beneath a vast broken arch whose keystone hangs by a thread. Fragments of carved garlands litter the paving. A strong draught moves through the arch with a low moan. The road runs east along its length, and the way back lies north.
rooms.1629: A shallow channel runs along the middle of the road, once a watercourse for some forgotten rite and now filled with black mud and reeds. Stone lions crouch at intervals along the verge, though weather has taken their manes and mouths. The air is damp, and the hum of the rift is only a murmur here. East the road meets a junction; west it bends.
rooms.1628: Flat paving stones, worn into a gentle dip, mark the line of the avenue between two broken walls. Scrubby grass grows in thin tufts along the margins, and a wind-twisted sapling clings to a crack. Scraps of blue glass glint in the dust where some window once stood. The junction lies a few paces east, and the road runs on west.
rooms.1607: The walkway begins here as a raised causeway of pale stone, its surface inlaid with row upon row of ancient bones set into the paving in strange patterns. Leg-bones and ribs form spirals, and skulls are set into the low walls like cobbles. The air is dry and sharp with the scent of old dust. The causeway runs east into the gloom and west to the plaza.
rooms.1618: The causeway turns here from the west toward the south, and the bones in the paving gather into the wide curve of a giant ribcage. Whitened tusks and horns are set upright along the wall like the teeth of some vast beast. A cold hum shivers through the stones. The walkway goes on south, and west runs back toward the plaza.
rooms.1619: The walkway runs straight between two walls built entirely of stacked skulls, row on row, grinning in the dim. Their hollows are stuffed with the pale dust of ages. The hum of the rift grows louder, almost a low chant. The causeway leads north toward the bend and south to a junction.
rooms.1620: Three doorways open from a small court where the walkway meets, each beneath a lintel of carved bone. They lead east to the Room of Elders, south to the Room of Bravery and west to the Room of Courage, while the walkway runs back north. A circle of old bronze is set into the ground, graven with a pattern of crossed swords. A hush hangs here, thick as felt.
rooms.1623: A long hall of cold stone, its walls lined with niches in which stone figures of bearded elders sit, hands folded on their knees. A single oil-black lamp hangs from the vaulted ceiling by a chain. Dust lies thick on the floor except along a line of footprints worn into the flags. A doorway east leads deeper, and the arch west returns to the walkway.
rooms.1624: This is a round chamber where a spiral stair of worn steps climbs the wall to an opening in the ceiling. Every step is hollowed in the middle by centuries of patient feet. Carved on the walls in ring after ring are tallies of trials endured, each stroke scratched by a different hand. Torch brackets stand empty. The only other way out is the arch to the west, and the stair leads up to the Room of Might.
rooms.1617: Great stone weights, anvils and iron-bound bars lie scattered across the floor of this high chamber, tests of strength left by champions long gone. The walls are thick with scratches counting lifts and throws. A wide arch to the north opens on the Way of Heroes, and a stair leads down to the Room of Perseverance. The air smells of cold iron.
rooms.1616: The Way of Heroes starts here as a wide avenue paved in blue-grey slabs, lined by statues of warriors in crested helms. A fountain basin, dry and cracked, stands against a ruined wall. Low arches at the south end of the street lead into the Room of Might. The avenue runs east into the ruin beneath a hard grey sky.
rooms.1613: Four stone braziers stand at the corners of a small crossing, each blackened inside by fires lit for forgotten feasts. A low doorway to the north opens into a Room of Slaying, its lintel carved with a ring of broken spears. The avenue runs on east and west, its paving scattered with rusted nails and splinters of old shafts.
rooms.1615: This low square chamber is a dead end, its walls hung with ancient trophy-racks that hold only splinters and rust. Great stains darken the floor in a ring. Carved beasts, all pierced by spears, run around the frieze. The only way out is the doorway south, back to the Way of Heroes.
rooms.1610: Slender pillars flank the avenue, each topped with a stone eagle with a broken beak. A doorway to the south leads into a Room of Slaying. Loose gravel and shards of pottery crunch underfoot. The avenue runs east and west along its line of columns.
rooms.1609: This wide crossroads on the Way of Heroes holds a great circle of pale flags laid out like a shield. Doors to the north and south open into two more rooms of Slaying, their lintels graven with spears. The avenue goes on east toward the junction and west along the line of columns. Wind whirls dust and dried leaves around the shield-circle.
rooms.1611: A cold small chamber of dark stone, its walls scored with rows of notches, each a tally of battles won. A stone table stands in the centre, stained and chipped. The air is stale and heavy. The only way out is the doorway south, which returns to the Way of Heroes.
rooms.1606: The Way of Heroes ends in a broad approach paved with mosaic, tiny tiles laid in the shape of a wreath and half lost to weather. A tall column with a cracked capital marks the edge, and beyond it the Junction of Ancients waits to the east. The road runs west along the avenue of heroes. Thin grass pushes through the mosaic.
rooms.1612: A narrow chamber where a long stone bench runs beneath a row of iron hooks, each hook once holding a trophy of some great kill. A thin shaft of light falls through a crack in the vault. The floor is gritty with ash. The only way out is the arch north, back to the Way of Heroes.
rooms.1614: Rough pillars stand in the corners of this small chamber of slaying, each wrapped in rusty chain. Pale scorch marks climb the walls in tongues. A heavy stone block, hollowed like a trough, stands in the middle, its rim chipped deeply. A doorway north returns to the Way of Heroes.
rooms.1621: A dim round chamber whose floor is laid with a mosaic of a lone figure facing a great dark mass, much of it lost under dust. Torch sconces hang empty. The ceiling is low and domed, black with the soot of vanished fires. The only way out is the doorway north, to the junction of the walkway.
rooms.1622: A bare, narrow chamber lit by a single slit that casts a blade of light across the floor. Along the walls are carved the names of those who faced death here, and some of the letters are still sharp. A cracked stone shield hangs on the far wall. The doorway east opens on the walkway junction.

1602.description: The statue shows a hero in a long robe, one hand open as if to welcome the traveller. The name on the plinth has been chiselled away.

1627.description: The pedestal once held a statue, for four bronze bolts still stand in its top. Around its rim runs a laurel wreath, cut with great care.

1639.description: The stone head is taller than a man, with a strong jaw and a worn crown. It seems to have fallen from some great statue long ago.

1607.description: The bones are set with strange care into spirals and rings. Whoever laid them meant the pattern to be walked.

1622.description: The names are cut in a dozen different hands. Beneath the last is a blank space, as if the wall were waiting.

creatures.long_desc: A bone sentry in rusted mail stands rigid on the paving, a notched spear in its hands.
creatures.description: A skeleton still bound in the corroded mail of some old guard. Pale fire gutters in its empty sockets as it turns to follow you.

creatures.long_desc: A hero's shade drifts above the stones, its pale hand tightening on a sword that is not there.
creatures.description: The faint outline of a warrior in an antique crested helm, thin as mist. It keeps the old trials and does not suffer the living to pass them unchallenged.

creatures.long_desc: A black raven perches on a broken column, watching you with a bright unblinking eye.
creatures.description: A big raven with feathers dusted white by the ruin. It pecks at the old bones in the paving and croaks at anything that comes near.

creatures.long_desc: A granite guardian stands in the doorway, its stone sword resting across its chest.
creatures.description: A statue of a heavy-browed warrior given terrible life by the rift. Dust trickles from its joints with every slow step.

creatures.long_desc: A slayer wraith circles the chamber, a spear of grey light in its fist.
creatures.description: The ghost of a hunter bound to the Rooms of Slaying, its body ragged smoke and its eyes hard as flint. It forever repeats the throw that killed it.

creatures.long_desc: Elder Verun, Keeper of Trials, stands beside the worn stair with a staff of pale bone.
creatures.description: The ghost of the eldest of the first heroes, bent and bearded, with eyes like cold lamps. He judges every traveller who comes to the stair, and finds most wanting.

creatures.long_desc: The Ancient Champion stands at the lip of the Rift, a vast blade of grey light held low at his side.
creatures.description: The greatest of the first heroes, a towering figure in antique plate, still keeping watch over the chasm. His voice is the hum of the rift itself, and his sword has not been lowered in a thousand years.

items.room_desc: A notched sentry spear lies here.
items.description: A long spear with a pitted iron head and a shaft gone dark with age. It is still well balanced.

items.room_desc: A bronze laurel circlet lies here.
items.description: A circlet of cast bronze leaves, green at the edges. It is cold even in the hand.

items.room_desc: A carved granite shard lies here.
items.description: A palm-sized piece of old statuary, with part of a stern stone face still cut into it. Collectors pay well for such relics.

items.room_desc: A worn silver signet ring lies here.
items.description: A heavy silver ring stamped with the seal of the first elders. It hums faintly with the rift.

items.room_desc: The Champion's grey greatsword lies here, humming softly.
items.description: A great blade of dull grey steel, etched with the names of the first heroes. It hums with the rift whenever it is drawn.
